text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to extract request normalizer + routing decision into a small service 'route-core'. I think this will reduce coupling between the runtime and policy layers.

jake: Can you sketch the boundaries? are we pulling any state out of the runtime (kv cache) or just logic?

maria: Short sketch:
- normalize incoming reqs (headers, client version, canonical forms)
- evaluate matching rules + weights
- return route + hints (cache key prefix, batch affinity)

priya: sounds promising. major risk is latency bump on hotpath. what's the expected p99 add?

maria: Target is <= 2ms median, <= 8ms p99 in colocated mode. We'll start with colocated (sidecar) and then offer networked mode.

sasha: Sidecar first is good. For networked mode we need fallbacks to runtime-local policy to survive partitions.

jake: For rollout: canary 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on >1.5x error rate or +10% p99. Agree?

maria: Agreed. Also plan to add feature flag and header to force old path.

arch-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7412 and checklist: design doc, prototype, perf harness, canary playbook, telemetry.

priya: Need to ensure we don't duplicate KV semantics. Suggest route-core returns cache key hints, not KV content. runtime stays authoritative for cache lookups.

maria: yes — route-core will be stateless. only deterministic hints. runtime owns KV store.

jake: test harness: small load generator and bench script.

```bash
# run route-core perf locally
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 route-core:local
wrk -t4 -c200 -d30s http://localhost:8080/route -s scripts/route.lua
```

sasha: metrics to watch: route_latency_p50/p95/p99, route_miss_rate, route_error_rate, runtime_cache_hit_by_hint.

maria: I'll draft a short design doc and link it here later. action items: maria write doc, jake build perf harness, priya add monitoring plan, sasha write canary playbook. target spike next sprint.

priya: +1

jake: +1

sasha: :thumbsup:
